description: Imports corporate travel booking records from the Navan booking-data API.

spec.apiVersionPinning: path segment `/v1` baked into the base URL constant; no version header or query param

credentialModes.name: OAuth2 client credentials (Navan API client id + secret)

continuity.notes: Pure read-only HTTP polling; the connector creates no server-side objects at Navan. Resumption is a datetime watermark held entirely in Flow connector state (ResourceState.Incremental.cursor); on restart the next sweep simply requests a wider updatedFrom..updatedTo window, so an arbitrarily long pause costs neither side anything beyond a larger catch-up page count. No retention window or resume-token expiry is referenced anywhere in the connector.

configFields.name: credentials.client_id
configFields.description: Navan API client id; see the Navan help-center booking-data-integration article linked from the config description.

configFields.name: name
configFields.description: Name of this resource (generic CDK ResourceConfig field).

configFields.name: interval
configFields.description: ISO-8601 duration between updates for this resource; CDK default PT0S, Navan ships PT5M for bookings.

schedules.role: polling interval for both the backfill sweep and the incremental sweep

params.page: <1-based page number, from the PageCursor in connector state>

authTierRationale: Exactly one credential mode is offered and it is OAuth2 client_credentials: the user must obtain and paste a client_id AND client_secret pair from Navan's admin console (booking-data integration setup) before the connector will run. ConnectorSpec sets oauth2=None, so there is NO hosted control-plane OAuth app doing the registration on the user's behalf and no browser consent redirect — the standalone tier is therefore T2, not T1. It is not T3: no refresh token is ever requested from the user; ClientCredentialsOAuth2Credentials carries only client_id/client_secret and the CDK mints a short-lived access token per run via the client_credentials grant. Borderline note: because it is a self-serve two-field secret pair rather than a redirect-URI OAuth app registration, this sits at the easy edge of T2 and a reader optimizing for user effort may reasonably see it as T1-adjacent.

unionMisfits.description: The incremental sweep writes a page loop (`while current_page <= total_pages`, incrementing current_page) but `total_pages` is initialized to 1 and is never reassigned from `response.page.totalPages`. The intended mechanism is unambiguously the same explicit-total page paginator as the backfill, yet the code as written terminates after page 1 and silently drops every later page of a multi-page change window. Neither {"type":"page",...} (describes intent, not runtime) nor {"type":"none"} (describes runtime, not intent) is truthful, so the field is abstained to null. The schema has no way to express 'declared paginator that is inert due to a defect'.

paginator.defectNote: loop bound never read from the response envelope; effective page count is 1

unionMisfits.description: The backfill request carries a time parameter (`updatedTo`) but it is an UPPER bound freezing the historical sweep at the cutoff, not a lower watermark that advances. `incrementalParam` in the schema only models the advancing lower bound, so the backfill's time-boxing is unrepresentable and is emitted as null, losing the fact that the backfill is time-bounded at all.

The incremental leg does not rely on the server's updatedFrom filter alone. It re-filters client-side (`modified_ts > cursor_timestamp` gates the yield) and separately tracks a max-seen watermark that becomes the new cursor. Records inside the requested window whose lastModified equals the old cursor are fetched but deliberately suppressed. The PullSpec union models only the request; it cannot express a post-fetch record filter or the max-of-lastModified cursor advancement rule.

proposedShape.cursorAdvance: max(record.lastModified) over the sweep, only if it exceeds the previous cursor

unionMisfits.description: One logical credential mode uses TWO different auth placements at two different endpoints, which the flat scheme union cannot hold at once. At the token endpoint the client_id:client_secret pair is sent as an HTTP Basic Authorization header (OAuth2ClientCredentialsPlacement.HEADERS, selected explicitly by the connector, overriding the CDK's FORM default), while the resulting access_token is sent to the data API as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The emitted oauth2 member records the grant and token URL but silently drops the Basic-at-token-endpoint placement.

The connector has one hostname but two distinct path roots on it: data requests go to https://api.navan.com/v1 while the token exchange goes to https://api.navan.com/ta-auth/oauth/token, which is NOT under /v1. `baseUrl` as a single constant implies every request hangs off it, which is false for the auth call.

The 5-minute interval is a discovery-time DEFAULT written into initial_config; the CDK ResourceConfig exposes `interval` as a user-editable per-binding field, so the real runtime schedule is whatever the customer left in the binding. The Schedule union states a value with no way to mark it as an overridable default versus a fixed connector behaviour.

streams[0].pull.backfill.recordsPath.snippet:
data: list[TData]
    page: Page | None = None

abstained.streams[0].pull.incremental.paginator: Set to null deliberately per rule 1. The incremental request sends `page` and `pageSize` and the envelope returns `page.totalPages`, so a page paginator with terminateOn explicit_total is clearly what was intended — but the loop bound `total_pages` is hardcoded to 1 at api.py:106 and never reassigned from the response, so at runtime exactly one page is ever fetched and any change window exceeding 100 bookings is silently truncated. Emitting `page` would assert pagination that does not happen; emitting `none` would assert an intent that is not in the code. Both failure modes are the silent-truncation kind rule 1 warns about, so the field is abstained and the full mechanism is recorded in unionMisfits[0].
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.scopes: No scope list appears anywhere in the connector or in the CDK's client_credentials token exchange (only grant_type plus the Basic-header client credentials are sent). Emitted as an empty list rather than guessing Navan's scope names.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.authUrl: There is no authorization/consent URL. The client_credentials grant is a direct server-to-server token POST; ConnectorSpec.oauth2 is None so no browser redirect URL exists to record.
abstained.streams[0].pull.backfill.incrementalPara: Null because the backfill's only time parameter (`updatedTo`) is a fixed upper bound derived from the cutoff, not an advancing lower watermark; see unionMisfits[1].
abstained.streams[0].writeDisposition: Inferred as `merge` from the declared document key ["/uuid"] plus the incremental leg re-emitting changed bookings under the same uuid. The connector never emits tombstones and never declares a disposition explicitly, so this is a reading of CDK convention rather than a stated fact.
abstained.execution.continuity.releasedOnShutdown: Null because the question does not apply — the connector creates no server-side artifacts to release.
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: Null: no static headers are set on the data session; the only header applied is the Authorization: Bearer added per-request by the CDK's TokenSource.
